Present petition has been filed recalling the order dated 27.02.2024 passed by learned trial Court in B.A. No. 150 of 2024 by which respondent i.e. Narendra Ojha has been granted bail.

The facts in brief are that FIR has been lodged at police station concerned to the effect that the prosecutrix was subjected to Gang rape by the respondent No. 2 along with co-accused persons and the respondent No. 2 had also prepared videography through mobile phone and also threatened the prosecutrix not to disclose the said incident of rape to anybody otherwise, he would kill her husband and son.
Thereafter, respondent No. 2 circulated the said video in the social media platform and had also extorted Rs. 2 Lakhs from the prosecutrix.

On the basis of aforesaid, FIR bearing crime No.
04/2024 was registered at police station Mahila Thana, District Shivpuri for the offence punishable under sections 376 (D), 384, 292, 506 of IPC.
During investigation, 2 MCRC-18130-2024 respondent was arrested.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that after getting released on bail, respondent No. 2 threatened the prosecutrix, thereby, breached the condition No. 2 of the bail order impugned,
therefore, present petition be allowed and the bail granted to the respondent No. 2 be cancelled.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 2 opposed the petition and prayed for dismissal of the petition on the ground that it has no sum and substance.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

This court vide order dated 02/08/2024 called status report from concerned police station and as per status report filed by the concerned police station after conducting enquiry and taking evidence of the witnesses, no such evidence of threatening is found.

It is well settled that very cogent and overwhelming circumstances or grounds are required to cancel the bail already granted and unless a 3 MCRC-18130-2024 strong case based on any supervening event is made out, an order granting bail is not to be lightly interfered with under Section 439 (2)
CrPC.
In this case, applicant has failed to show any cogent, overwhelming circumstances or ground.
Under these circumstances, there is no reason to recall the order granting bail to the respondent No.
Consequently, the present application, seeking cancellation of bail granted to the respondent No. 2 vide impugned order, sans merit and is hereby dismissed.
Certified copy as per rules.
